title: Finite generators for the ideal multiplication kernel over a Noetherian algebra
statement: Let R and S be Noetherian commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], M a finite S-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], phi:R->S a ring map, and I an ideal of R. Give M its R-action through phi and M tensor_R I its S-action on M. Let mu:I tensor_R M->M be multiplication, and e:M tensor_R I->I tensor_R M the tensor symmetry. There is a finite subset s of M tensor_R I such that mu(e(k))=0 for every k in s, and every k with mu(e(k))=0 lies in span_S(s).

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00R6, proof from choosing a fixed index through vanishing of the Tor transition map; Remark 00M6. Official text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00R6.

proof.text: Choose finite spanning sets X of M over S and Y of I over R. The set of x tensor y with x in X and y in Y is finite. Span induction in each variable shows it spans M tensor_R I over S: x tensor a*y = phi(a)*(x tensor y). Tensor induction then proves the span is the whole tensor product.

The map pi=mu composed with symmetry is S-linear: pi(b*x tensor a)=phi(a)*b*x=b*pi(x tensor a), with additivity and tensor induction extending this to all tensors. Its kernel is a submodule of the finite S-module just constructed. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] and extract a finite spanning set of the kernel. Membership in the kernel gives the claimed zero equations.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_tensor_kernel_generators
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {M : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [AddCommGroup M]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [Module S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (φ : R →+* S) (I : Ideal R) :
    letI := Module.compHom M φ
    letI : SMulCommClass R S M := ⟨fun a b x ↦ smul_comm (φ a) b x⟩
    let μ := TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.lsmul R M).comp I.subtype)
    ∃ s : Finset (M ⊗[R] I),
      (∀ k ∈ s, μ (TensorProduct.comm R M I k) = 0) ∧
      (∀ k : M ⊗[R] I, μ (TensorProduct.comm R M I k) = 0 →
        k ∈ Submodule.span S (s : Set (M ⊗[R] I)))
